title: Fixed-location time references did not show an extra annual dispersion reduction from a shallow earthquake filter in 2001-2025
abstract: We tested a reported decrease in annual earthquake count variation after a 100 km, 30 day predecessor filter. We used the same ComCat M5.5+ snapshot, depths 0-70 km, and 25 scored years. We kept each event location and year and replaced its time independently within its year or month. The filter retained 6,629 of 10,051 observed events. Annual variance divided by mean was 2.265. The difference from the expected value for equal-size uniform removal was -5.886. In 999 yearly time references this difference had a central 95% range of -6.541 to -5.698, with lower-tail rank 0.871. The monthly range was -6.076 to -5.747, with rank 0.637. Raw filtered dispersion was below the yearly reference, but within the monthly range. Thus the extra reduction relative to uniform removal was not unusual under these references. This does not refute local triggering. It shows that a uniform-removal control alone cannot separate short-time event clustering from annual spatial rate variation and filter selection. One snapshot, fixed windows, 25 years and conditional reference assumptions limit inference.

display.caption: Filtered annual dispersion and its difference from the equal-count removal expectation. References keep exact locations and years and replace times within each year or month. The black line is the observed value. The ranges are conditional reference ranges, not confidence intervals.

citations.reason: We reuse its source snapshot and filter definition. We add fixed-location yearly and monthly time references. Data overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
Its annual spatial alignment test provides context for keeping spatial annual rates fixed.
